subject: Life Skills
title: Scheduling Rest
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Scheduling Rest.

hook.text: She put rest last on her list — after every task was done. It never came. She burned out by March.

buildup.text: Treating rest as a reward means it only arrives when you feel you have earned it. That moment rarely comes.

discovery.text: Rest is not a reward. It is an input. Athletes schedule recovery because performance depends on it.

twist.text: You do not have time for rest is the same logic as 'I do not have time to sharpen the axe.' It costs more later.

climax.text: Block rest on your calendar with the same respect as a meeting. If it is not scheduled, it will not happen.

punchline.text: Schedule your rest or your body will schedule it for you.

quiz.question: Why should rest be scheduled, not earned?
options: Because people forget to relax otherwise
Because rest is an input for performance, not a reward after it
Because scheduled rest is more enjoyable
